signs: Sudden, sharp, intense belly pain
Feeling very dizzy or fainting
Feeling sick, with possible or known early pregnancy
Shoulder tip pain (can mean internal bleeding)
Belly pain low on one side in early pregnancy (weeks 4 to 12)
Vaginal bleeding unlike a normal period (watery, dark brown, on and off)
Pain when pooping or peeing, or diarrhoea, when you might be pregnant

condition: Postpartum hemorrhage (first 24 hours up to 12 weeks after birth)
signs: Heavy bleeding soaking one or more pads in an hour
Clots bigger than an egg or golf ball, or passing tissue
Dizziness, blurred vision or feeling faint
Racing heart, fast breathing, pale or clammy skin
Pain or swelling in the vagina or perineum
Severe headache
Vision changes (blurring, temporary vision loss, light sensitivity)
Severe pain in the upper belly under the right ribs
Severe shortness of breath
Sudden swelling of the face or hands

condition: Postpartum preeclampsia (most within 48 hours, can be up to 6 weeks or later after birth)
signs: Severe headache
Vision changes
Pain in the upper belly under the right ribs
Nausea and vomiting
Shortness of breath
Reduced urination
Blood pressure 140/90 or higher

condition: Postpartum psychosis with risk of harm
signs: Thoughts of harming yourself or the baby
Hallucinations or delusions with risk of imminent harm

condition: Suspected postpartum psychosis (usually within 2 weeks of birth)
signs: Hearing, seeing or feeling things that are not there
Unusual fears or beliefs
Feeling unusually high, racing thoughts, restlessness
Rapidly changing moods or severe low mood
Significant confusion
Confusion or slurred speech
Blue, grey, pale or blotchy skin, lips or tongue
Rash that does not fade under a glass
Difficulty breathing or very fast breathing
Large areas of peeling skin

condition: Possible toxic shock syndrome (remove any tampon or menstrual cup)
signs: High temperature or shivering with muscle aches
Vomiting or diarrhoea
Sandpaper-like rash
Bright red palms, soles, tongue or eye whites
Feeling dizzy or confused

condition: Severe dehydration from vomiting in pregnancy (hyperemesis gravidarum)
signs: Cannot keep any food or fluid down and vomiting for 24 hours or more
Unable to drink for more than 8 hours or eat for more than 24 hours
Light-headedness, rapid heartbeat
Vomiting every day that is getting more frequent
Losing a lot of weight
Vomiting stopping you eating or drinking normally
